marta: Heads-up — between 09:06 and 09:18 UTC we saw a big SCIM provisioning surge from a couple of large customers. ~70% 429s and intermittent KMS decrypt errors. Deprovision flows are blocked for ~30 users. Pasting a representative log snippet below.

marta: ```
2026-03-18T09:07:12Z ERROR scim-provisioner request_id=abcd1234 status=429 retries=3 payload={...} error=ProvisionRateExceeded
2026-03-18T09:07:13Z ERROR kms-decrypt request_id=abcd1234 key=alias/primary-kms error=InvalidCiphertextException context_mismatch=true
2026-03-18T09:07:14Z WARN deprovisioner user_id=U12345 state=stuck
```

alex: ack. did we hit KMS quota or key policy? any recent key rotation on primary-kms?

ryan: I queried CloudWatch for the key usage spike — looks like sudden burst of Decrypt API calls at the same time as the SCIM replay. Not a 403, more like InvalidCiphertextException + Throttling on KMS metrics.

lena: could be replayed requests with stale ciphertext/context. SCIM provider sometimes retries without preserving encryption context headers. That would cause InvalidCiphertext.

marta: right — audit logs show many provisioning requests missing the `encryption_context: {tenant_id}` field. That breaks our KMS envelope checks.

alex: temporary mitigation: pause SCIM retry worker for affected customers and enable exponential backoff at edge. We can also flip to `alias/secondary-kms` which has higher quota, but policy requires approval.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042. Pager duty notified.

ryan: I can patch the SCIM client to drop immediate retries and add jitter. Quick rollback will reduce Decrypt QPS. I have a short changelist: 
```
PATCH: scim/client.go
- retry: immediate up to 3
+ retry: exponential backoff jitter
```

lena: also need to handle malformed encryption headers defensively: if context missing, fail-provision with clear audit reason instead of requeueing. That prevents repeated bad decrypt attempts.

marta: Agreed. Security/compliance wants a backfill plan for audit gaps — we have ~120 events with missing context for the last 48h. @security-audit-bot can we export the raw provisioning records for review?

security-audit-bot: Export job queued: AUDIT-EXPORT-171945. ETA ~18m. Note: exports include redaction markers per PII policy.

alex: For immediate recovery, propose 2 steps: 1) reduce SCIM concurrency to 10% for affected orgs 2) patch client to stop retries. That should drop KMS decrypt QPS under threshold in ~5m.

marta: Oncall — can you run a one-off key usage increase request to KMS service team? We might need a temporary quota bump if retries have already burned through allowances.

ryan: sent support ticket to cloud provider (SUP-7892) with graph and request. They replied with acknowledgement and suggested we move non-critical decrypts to a secondary alias while they increase soft limits.

lena: compliance note — switching aliases requires audit entry and approval. If we do a temporary alias fallback, we must record the reason and timeframe. I'll draft the entry.

marta: adding action items: 
- reduce SCIM concurrency for affected orgs (alex)
- patch client retry/backoff & defensive header check (ryan)
- request KMS soft quota bump (marta)
- prepare audit backfill and export (lena + security-audit-bot)
- don't switch alias without approval; if we must, record in audit and notify Legal (lena)

alex: starting the concurrency throttle now. Will post logs once QPS drops.

ryan: deploying retry/backoff patch to canary in 2m.

marta: thanks. once we confirm KMS error rate drops, we'll re-run deprovision backlog. Please post any blocker updates here. :thumbsup:
